attributes.body:
Verb + てもいい is a construction in Japanese used to express that something is 'okay', or 'alright'. It can also be used as a question to ask if you 'can', or 'may' do something.

This phrase is also regularly used without the も, but is considered a bit more direct/casual. It is best to remove the も only when talking to people that you know well.

This expression is simply a construction that literally means て (verb) も (also) いい (is good).

Caution

As this grammar point uses the て form of verbs, it is important to remember that some verbs will use で instead of て.

attributes.description: TE-form verb + MO II DESU KA
May / Can I do ~? Can I use?

attributes.body: Both Verb + てもいい and てもかまわない are used to give or ask for permission. The difference is tone and formality. てもいい is a basic, everyday expression, while てもかまわない is slightly more formal and often used in writing or professional contexts to mean 'It doesn't matter if…' or 'It's fine if…'

second_relatable.title: てもかまわない
second_relatable.meaning: It doesn't matter if, I don't mind

attributes.body: The ても form means 'even if.' One common use is Verb + てもいい, which gives or asks for permission (e.g. 食べてもいい？ = 'Can I eat this?') A related pattern is でよければ, which uses the conditional form of いい (よければ) to mean 'if it's okay.' It's often used to make polite offers, like 私でよければお手伝いします ('If I'm okay [as a choice], I'll help').

first_relatable.title: でよければ
first_relatable.meaning: If it is alright, If you don't mind, If you would like, If possible

second_relatable.title: Verb + てもいい
second_relatable.meaning: It's okay to, It's alright to, Can/may

attributes.body: The Verb + て form is used to connect a verb to another verb, or another part of the sentence. When combined with もいい (meaning 'even' + 'good' or 'okay'), it asks for or grants permission. For example, 食べてもいい？with a question mark means 'Can I eat this?' (literally, 'Is it okay even if I eat this?'), while 食べてもいい with no question mark means 'you can eat it.'

first_relatable.title: Verb + てもいい
first_relatable.meaning: It's okay to, It's alright to, Can/may

attributes.body: The てもいい pattern expresses that something is acceptable or allowed. With verbs, it's used to give or ask for permission, such as 食べてもいい？ (Can I eat this?') It can also be used with nouns or adjectives to ask if a condition is acceptable, like 冷たくてもいい? ('Is it okay if it's cold?) when referring to a drink, for example.

second_relatable.title: てもいい
second_relatable.meaning: It is alright/fine/okay even if, Can/may, ~ is also okay

attributes.body: The ても form has the core meaning of 'even if.' One common use is Verb + てもいい, which gives or asks for permission—for example, 食べてもいいですか？ literally means 'Is it okay even if I eat this?' but works like 'Can/May I eat this?' in English. Similarly, といってもいい means 'It's okay even if you say...' but is used to express 'You could say' or 'One might say.'

attributes.body: ても has the core meaning of 'even if.' One common use is in Verb + てもいい to ask or give permission. For example, 食べてもいいですか？ means 'Can/May I eat this?' (literally, 'Is it okay even if I eat this?') More broadly, ても can also express contrast. For example, 寒くても行きます means 'I'll go even if it's cold.'
